messages.author: decd30055c435d87
messages.subject: Scale not obeying limits?
parts:
Hello, I'm trying to plot bars but they are disobeying my limits
commands. (Insolent bars!) Here is the data:

foo <- structure(list(year = c(2009, 2009, 2009, 2010, 2010, 2010, 2011,
2011, 2011), grade = c(6, 7, 8, 6, 7, 8, 6, 7, 8), readprob = c(0.100029,
0.0996918, 0.0765892, 0.124111, 0.0777718, 0.0663743, 0.120688,
0.110797, 0.0594606)), .Names = c("year", "grade", "readprob"
), class = "data.frame", row.names = c("2909", "2910", "2911",
"2912", "2913", "2914", "2915", "2916", "2917"))

The code I'm running is:
ggplot(data=foo, aes(x=grade, y=100*mathprob))+
geom_bar(stat="identity")+
scale_x_discrete(name="Probability of Exceeding Standards",
limits=c(6, 8), breaks=c(6, 7, 8), labels=c(6, 7, 8), drop=T) +
scale_y_continuous(name="Probability of Exceeding Standards",
limits=c(0, 35))+
opts(title="Probability of Exceeding Standards in Grade 8 Math")+
facet_grid(. ~ year)

I expected to get three bars, one for each grade (6, 7, 8) approximately
centered in each panel. But what I get is three bars jammed in on the
right, with blank space where bars for the non-existent grades 1:5 would
be.

Any idea why this should be so?

TIA.

--
Stuart Luppescu

parts:
On 03/28/2012 05:23 PM, Stuart Luppescu wrote:
Sorry, I got my datasets mixed up. The y variable is readprob, not
mathprob. Here is the corrected code.

ggplot(data=foo, aes(x=grade, y=100*readprob))+

geom_bar(stat="identity")+
scale_x_discrete(name="Probability of Exceeding Standards", limits=c(6,
8), breaks=c(6, 7, 8), labels=c(6, 7, 8), drop=T) +
scale_y_continuous(name="Probability of Exceeding Standards",
limits=c(0, 35))+

opts(title="Probability of Exceeding Standards in Grade 8 Reading")+
facet_grid(. ~ year)

ggplot2 does a pretty nice job of setting the limits on plots so I
altered you code just a little but I think this might be what you are
looking for:

ggplot(data=foo, aes(x=grade, y=100*readprob))+
geom_bar(stat="identity")+
scale_x_discrete(name="Probability of Exceeding Standards") +
scale_y_continuous(name="Probability of Exceeding Standards")+

opts(title="Probability of Exceeding Standards in Grade 8 Math")+
